scraped.scraped_description: Pear loads applications remotely from peers and allows anyone to create and share applications with peers.

name: Pear by Holepunch
tagline: A peer-to-peer runtime, development and deployment platform for building unstoppable applications
dependency_risks: Dependency on Bare runtime for cross-platform functionality
documented_limitations: Platform is described as having experimental and unstable modules
Documentation indicates some modules are new and untested
failure_modes: Network partition failures in peer-to-peer architecture
contributor_governance: Open source contribution model with maintainer oversight
political_relevance_summary: Pear addresses the centralization of internet infrastructure by providing peer-to-peer runtime tools that could enable censorship-resistant civic applications, though its primary focus is developer tooling rather than direct civic use.

movement_building_utility.notes: Pear by Holepunch provides digital rights infrastructure that underpins civic freedoms online.

generalizability_notes: High generalizability. Pear by Holepunch is open source and already deployed across multiple countries/jurisdictions, making replication straightforward for other contexts.

self_hosting_capability.notes: Peer-to-peer runtime — applications built on Pear are inherently self-hosted and peer-distributed. No central server required for deployment or operation.
